MAAG: MAAG — Military Assistance Advisory Group (U.S. advisory mission).
MACV: MACV — Military Assistance Command, Vietnam (U.S. command in Vietnam).
ARVN: ARVN — Army of the Republic of Vietnam (South Vietnamese army).
NVA: NVA — North Vietnamese Army (regular forces of North Vietnam).
DMZ: DMZ — Demilitarized Zone (border zone between North and South Vietnam).
KIA: KIA — Killed in Action (military casualty classification).
MIA: MIA — Missing in Action (personnel unaccounted for).
POW: POW — Prisoner of War (captured military personnel).
USMC: USMC — United States Marine Corps (military branch).
USAF: USAF — United States Air Force (military branch).
ROK: ROK — Republic of Korea (South Korea; allied military forces in the Vietnam War).
R&R: R&R — Rest and Recuperation (leave period for military personnel).
FOB: FOB — Forward Operating Base (tactical military base).
FSB: FSB - Fire Support Base (tactical military base).
PAVN: PAVN — People's Army of Vietnam (official name for North Vietnam's military).
DRV: DRV — Democratic Republic of Vietnam (North Vietnam).
NLF: NLF — National Liberation Front (political/military organization commonly called the Viet Cong).
PRG: PRG — Provisional Revolutionary Government (southern communist political authority formed during the war).
CORDS: CORDS — Civil Operations and Revolutionary Development Support (U.S.-South Vietnamese pacification program).
CIDG: CIDG — Civilian Irregular Defense Group (local forces organized with U.S. Special Forces support).
SOG: SOG — Studies and Observations Group (U.S. special operations unit, MACV-SOG).
LRRP: LRRP — Long-Range Reconnaissance Patrol (small deep-recon units).
TOC: TOC — Tactical Operations Center (unit command and control center).
RTO: RTO — Radio Telephone Operator (soldier handling communications).
PBR: PBR — Patrol Boat, River (U.S. Navy riverine patrol craft).
VCI: VCI — Viet Cong Infrastructure (covert communist political/support network).
DEROS: DEROS — Date Eligible for Return from Overseas (scheduled rotation date for personnel).
MEDCAP: MEDCAP — Medical Civic Action Program (military medical outreach to civilian populations).
COSVN: COSVN — Central Office for South Vietnam (communist headquarters directing southern operations).
APC: APC — Armored Personnel Carrier (tracked vehicle for troop transport).
CAP: CAP — Combined Action Platoon (U.S. Marines and Vietnamese militia living in villages).
SEATO: SEATO — Southeast Asia Treaty Organization (regional defense alliance).
VNAF: VNAF — Vietnamese Air Force (South Vietnam's air force).
CCN: CCN — Command and Control North (MACV-SOG forward element for operations into Laos and North Vietnam).
TAOR: TAOR — Tactical Area of Responsibility (assigned operational zone for a military unit).
RPG: RPG — Rocket-Propelled Grenade (shoulder-fired anti-armor weapon widely used by NVA/VC).
SITREP: SITREP — Situation Report (periodic battlefield status update).
MEDEVAC: MEDEVAC — Medical Evacuation (helicopter transport of wounded personnel).
CINC: CINC — Commander in Chief (top military commander of a unified command).
CINCPAC: CINCPAC — Commander in Chief, Pacific (head of U.S. Pacific Command).
PSYOP: PSYOP — Psychological Operations (propaganda and influence campaigns).
REMF: REMF — Rear Echelon Mother F***** (slang for non-combat support personnel).
CIB: CIB — Combat Infantryman Badge (award for infantry soldiers in combat).
DSHK: DShK — Degtyaryov-Shpagin Krupnokaliberny (Soviet heavy machine gun used by NVA).
AO: AO — Area of Operations (designated zone for military activity).
ANGLICO: ANGLICO — Air and Naval Gunfire Liaison Company (unit coordinating fire support).
SERE: SERE — Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape (military training program).
DASC: DASC — Direct Air Support Center (facility coordinating close air support missions).
JUSPAO: JUSPAO — Joint United States Public Affairs Office (U.S. information and media relations in Saigon).
ICTZ: ICTZ — I Corps Tactical Zone (northernmost military region of South Vietnam).
CHICOM: CHICOM — Chinese Communist (designation for weapons and materiel supplied by China to NVA/VC).
WP: WP — White Phosphorus (incendiary munition used for marking and screening).
NDP: NDP — Night Defensive Position (temporary perimeter set up for overnight security).
CONEX: CONEX — Container Express (standard military shipping container used for storage and fortification).
USARV: USARV — United States Army, Vietnam (administrative command for U.S. Army forces in Vietnam).
SLAM: SLAM — Search, Locate, Annihilate, and Monitor (aggressive patrol and interdiction tactic).
DIOCC: DIOCC — District Intelligence and Operations Coordination Center (combined intelligence hub at district level).
FAC: FAC — Forward Air Controller (pilot or ground observer directing close air support strikes).
WIA: WIA — Wounded in Action (military casualty classification for non-fatal injuries).
CAS: CAS — Close Air Support (air strikes against targets near friendly ground forces).
MAF: MAF — Marine Amphibious Force (major Marine Corps tactical formation in Vietnam).
MSR: MSR — Main Supply Route (primary road or trail used for logistics and resupply).
PF: PF — Popular Forces (South Vietnamese village-level militia).
RF: RF — Regional Forces (South Vietnamese province-level territorial military units).
HES: HES — Hamlet Evaluation System (U.S. reporting system measuring pacification progress in Vietnamese hamlets).
STABO: STABO — Stabilized Tactical Airborne Body Operations (helicopter extraction harness for personnel recovery).
PACAF: PACAF — Pacific Air Forces (U.S. Air Force major command responsible for air operations in the Pacific theater).
MACVSOG: MACV-SOG — Military Assistance Command, Vietnam – Studies and Observations Group (joint unconventional warfare task force).
BDA: BDA — Bomb Damage Assessment (post-strike evaluation of target destruction).
DFC: DFC — Distinguished Flying Cross (military decoration for heroism or achievement in aerial flight).
OPLAN: OPLAN — Operations Plan (detailed military plan for conducting operations).
RSSZ: RSSZ — Rung Sat Special Zone (VC-controlled mangrove swamp southeast of Saigon).
MRF: MRF — Mobile Riverine Force (joint Army-Navy force operating in the Mekong Delta).
TACAN: TACAN — Tactical Air Navigation (radio navigation system used by military aircraft).
RIF: RIF — Reconnaissance in Force (offensive patrol to locate and engage the enemy).
IFFV: IFFV — I Field Force, Vietnam (U.S. Army corps-level command for II Corps Tactical Zone).
TASS: TASS — Tactical Air Support Squadron (Air Force unit providing close air support coordination).
CTZ: CTZ — Corps Tactical Zone (one of four military regions dividing South Vietnam).
DIA: DIA — Defense Intelligence Agency (U.S. military intelligence organization involved in Vietnam War assessments).
EOD: EOD — Explosive Ordnance Disposal (military unit specializing in disarming munitions and booby traps).
FDC: FDC — Fire Direction Center (element computing firing data for artillery batteries).
GVN: GVN — Government of Vietnam (South Vietnamese government, often used in official U.S. documents).
HUMINT: HUMINT — Human Intelligence (intelligence gathered from human sources and agents).
JPRC: JPRC — Joint Personnel Recovery Center (MACV element coordinating search and rescue for downed aircrews and POWs).
LAW: LAW — Light Anti-tank Weapon (M72 disposable rocket launcher used by U.S. infantry).
NAVFORV: NAVFORV — Naval Forces, Vietnam (U.S. Navy command overseeing naval operations in Vietnamese waters).
SAM: SAM — Surface-to-Air Missile (anti-aircraft missile, notably the Soviet SA-2 used to defend North Vietnam).
TF: TF — Task Force (temporary military grouping organized for a specific mission or operation).
AWOL: AWOL — Absent Without Leave (military classification for unauthorized absence).
ROE: ROE — Rules of Engagement (guidelines governing the use of force).
NCO: NCO — Non-Commissioned Officer (military rank for enlisted leaders).
CO: CO — Commanding Officer (officer in command of a military unit).
FUBAR: FUBAR — Fouled Up Beyond All Recognition (slang for situation in disarray).
SNAFU: SNAFU — Situation Normal: All Fouled Up (slang indicating typical chaos).
CSS: CSS — Combat Service Support (logistical and administrative support activities).
ECM: ECM — Electronic Countermeasure (methods to jam or deceive enemy electronic systems).
EW: EW — Electronic Warfare (use of electromagnetic spectrum in combat operations).
JCS: JCS — Joint Chiefs of Staff (group of senior military leaders advising U.S. government).
